name: Panama Canal
hook: A French failure turned American triumph — the ditch that bent the map and made the trip east.

facts.statement: Nicknamed "The Big Ditch," the canal opened in 1914 and marked its centennial in 2014; Woodrow Wilson formally dedicated it in 1920.

facts.label: Gatun Lake
facts.statement: Gatun Lake, a man-made lake covering nearly 170 square miles, stores the water that keeps the locks running through the dry season.

facts.label: east, not west
facts.statement: Ships climb a staircase of locks; because Central America curves, a trip from the Pacific to the Atlantic actually heads east.

facts.label: Ferdinand de Lesseps
facts.statement: Ferdinand de Lesseps, who had built the Suez Canal, tried and failed here; his company went bankrupt, and the U.S. finished the job.

facts.label: Colón and Balboa
facts.statement: The canal's two port cities, Colón at the Caribbean end and Balboa at the Pacific end, are named for explorers.

facts.label: the Caribbean Sea
facts.statement: The canal's Atlantic entrance opens into the Caribbean, which the canal helped make one of the world's most traveled seas.

facts.label: Cape Horn and Magellan
facts.statement: Before the canal, ships rounded Cape Horn or threaded the Strait of Magellan; even today, supertankers too big for the locks take the long way.
